Crieth
krī'eth
v. (third person singular of cry: to call out, to appeal aloud; rendering Hebrew tsa'aq, za'aq, qara')
Old French crier, from Latin quiritare, to wail or to call upon the citizens for help. The Hebrew tsa'aq is the shriek of one under injustice, and it is a legal appeal as much as a sound.

Biblical Definition

The first cry in Scripture comes from the ground: “the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground” (Gen 4:10). Blood unjustly shed has a voice, and God hears it whether or not any man does — which is the foundation of every doctrine of divine justice. The law then attaches the same word to the poor man's pledge: if you take a man's garment for a pledge, restore it before sundown, “when he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious” (Exo 22:27). God appoints Himself the hearer of the cry of the man with no advocate. So the King is described: “he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper” (Psa 72:12). The soul of the wounded crieth out from the city, and God layeth not folly to them (Job 24:12). And the saint's cry is homesickness for God Himself: “my heart and my flesh crieth out for the living God” (Psa 84:2). Finally wisdom cries: “Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets” (Pro 1:20) — God is not silent, and men perish under a preaching they have heard.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines to cry as to utter a loud voice; to call importunately; to implore; to exclaim in distress or supplication; and, of a herald, to proclaim.

expand to see more

CRY, v.i. To utter a loud voice; to speak, call or exclaim with vehemence.

2. To call importunately; to utter a loud voice, with earnestness; to implore; to supplicate.

3. To utter a loud voice in weeping; to lament; to shed tears with audible sound.

Key Scripture

Gen 4:10 — "And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground."

Psa 72:12 — "For he shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also, and him that hath no helper."

Pro 1:20 — "Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets:"

Modern Corruption

The cry of the oppressed has been annexed to political programmes as an autonomous claim, and detached from the God who alone said He would hear it.

expand to see more

The Bible is emphatic that God hears the cry of the poor, the widow, the fatherless, the stranger, and the man whose blood is in the ground, and it never treats that cry as a small matter. Exodus 22:27 puts the divine character behind it: when he crieth unto me, I will hear; for I am gracious. What has happened in modern usage is not that the cry has been amplified but that it has been detached. The categories of Scripture — the poor, the afflicted, the oppressed, the widow, the orphan — are covenantal categories under a God who judges, and the cry is addressed to Him; that is what makes it a claim rather than a grievance. Reassigned to a purely political frame, the cry becomes a bare demand backed by whatever power can be mustered, and it loses two things immediately: the certainty of being heard, and the standard by which a just remedy could be recognised. The church must not answer this by growing cold toward the cry, which would be a graver error than the one it corrects; Proverbs 21:13 warns the man who stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor that he shall cry himself and not be heard. It answers by keeping the cry addressed where Genesis 4:10 addressed it — unto me, from the ground.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tsa'aq (H6817) and za'aq (H2199), to cry out for help, to shriek under oppression; qara' (H7121), to call, to proclaim; ranan (H7442), to cry aloud, as Wisdom in the street.

expand to see more

Hebrew tsa'aq (H6817) — to cry out, to call for help; the blood from the ground and Israel's cry in Egypt; Genesis 4:10, Exodus 3:7.

Hebrew za'aq (H2199) — to shriek, to cry out in distress; the recurring verb of the judges cycle, when Israel cried unto the LORD; Judges 3:9, Psalm 22:5.

Hebrew ranan (H7442) — to cry aloud, to shout for joy; Wisdom lifting her voice in the streets; Proverbs 1:20, 8:3.

Usage

"“The voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground” — the first cry, and the ground of all divine justice."

"“When he crieth unto me, that I will hear; for I am gracious” — God as the hearer of the man with no advocate."

"“Wisdom crieth without” — God is not silent; men perish under a preaching they have heard."
